scoring: Any 'yes' is a red flag -> refer the child for diagnosis and treatment (RBSK -> District Early Intervention Centre).
result_logic: red_flag_count == 0 -> typical; 1 red flag -> monitor; >= 2 red flags -> refer
source: Navchetana: National Framework for Early Childhood Stimulation 2024, Annexure II (pp. 81-85)

items.question: Did you experience any complications during your pregnancy? For example, high blood pressure, diabetes, anemia, or diseases like measles, mumps, or rubella?
Did you experience any of the following complications during childbirth? For example: very long delivery, surgery, forceps delivery, premature delivery, or baby born with low birth weight?
Did the child have any problems at birth or soon after? For example, delayed birth cry, jaundice, blueness, or high fever?
Was the colour of the child unusual at birth? (Blue / Yellow / Pale)
Did the child have feeding difficulties such as suckling or swallowing during mother's feeding?
Has the child ever had fits or lost consciousness since birth?
Do the child's eyes frequently turn red or water?
Is there frequent pus or watery discharge from the child's ears?
Does the child frequently complain about ear aches or headaches?
Does the child have any missing or deformed body parts?
Is the child too small or too weak compared to other children of similar age?
Does the child's body have uncoordinated or jerky movements, or does the child have poor balance while walking?
Does the child walk with a limp?
Can the child not walk, or did the child start walking much later than other children?
Is there a lump or bump on the child's backbone?
Do the child's eyes squint?
Are the pupils of the child's eyes gray or white?
Does the child often bang into objects while walking, or do they fall frequently? Do they have difficulty seeing at night?
Are the child's ears deformed or missing?
Move any object (such as a toy or pen) about 12–20 inches in front of the child and within their visual field. Does the child fail to move their head with the movement of the object?

Take a rattle, bell, or utensil about 1–3 feet from the child's ear (ensure the child is not looking toward you) and make a sound by shaking or banging it. Does the child fail to turn their head toward the source of the sound?
Does the child show no big smiles or other warm, joyful expressions by 6 months?
Has the child NOT yet supported their own neck by 6 months?
Has the child NOT yet turned from belly to back and back to belly by 7–8 months?
Has the child NOT yet sat without support by 9 months?
Does the child NOT yet provide back-and-forth responses with sounds, smiles, or other facial expressions by 9 months?
Has the child NOT yet made babbling sounds like 'ba ba', 'ma ma', or 'da da' by 12 months?
Does the child NOT yet respond to their own name by 12 months?
Has the child NOT yet made back-and-forth gestures such as pointing, showing, reaching, or waving by 12 months?
Has the child NOT yet spoken a few words by 16 months?
Has the child NOT yet walked without support by 18 months?
Does the child NOT yet follow simple instructions such as 'come here' or 'give me the glass' by 18 months?
Has the child NOT yet spoken a few words by 24 months?
Can the child NOT yet say their own name by 3 years?
Has the child NOT yet achieved toilet control by 4 years?
Does the child NOT yet avoid simple hazards by 4 years?
Does the child NOT yet eat by themselves by 4 years?
Does the child NOT yet dress up on their own by 5 years?
